comments.text:
Players had spent nearly a decade hearing about Aqua's struggle, and finally seeing her reunited with Terra and Ventus, and ultimately leaving the Realm of Darkness was a huge moment of closure. Aqua wasn't just a story figure; she became playable during the final sequences, giving fans a chance to experience her combat style again, complete with her signature magic and keyblade abilities. Her arrival carried a lot of symbolic weight, the light of her keyblade literally breaking through darkness, visually showing hope prevailing.
Fans had theorized and hoped for her return for years. KH3 made it feel earned rather than sudden, which was satisfying for long-time followers.
comments.author: @mysticalgirljay

comments.text:
I mean, sure it was definitely impactful for being the first, but MY moment was Roxas's return. Being in love with "Days" (as the DS was my only console just as the GBA was) Roxas's story nobody can argue was THE most emotional of all. Everyone & everything he knew disappeared, even one of his best friends got completely erased from existence. And then, when he finally had enough (and pulled both of the best keyblades ever besides WtD) and tried to do something, he got captured and brainwashed into a false life for 3 days (Matrix style) only to remember all the pain right at the last moments, and have to merge with some other boy at the end? THAT'S tragedy. 😢💯

BUT when he used the power of light to travel many worlds away (something Sora or Mickey can't even do){btw only character seen to ever do the same was Yen Sid} just to scream "HANDS OFF MY FRIENDS" was the most emotional I've been in a long time. Only game to make me cry that much was the ending to Crisis Core. IYKYK 😭😭😭

It's left such an impact, i have the nobody symbol tattooed on my right forearm. Was my 3rd of 5 tats. Rocks this is definitely the best KH character 🫂💜🎮🕹️💯
